title: Bidirectional Dijkstra in Helsinki: Faster Routes!
description: Watch how Bidirectional Dijkstra visualizes shortest paths by expanding from both start and goal simultaneously. On a real street-map style graph of Helsinki (Kallio), the search converges quickly to reveal the optimal route.
ig_caption:
🗺️🚦 Helsinki (Kallio) street-map vibes—now with *Bidirectional Dijkstra*! 

Here’s the core idea: instead of running Dijkstra only from the start, we run two synchronized searches—one forward from the source and one backward from the destination. Each side maintains its own priority queue (min-heap) and distance labels, and the algorithm stops when the frontiers meet at a node where the best known combined path is proven minimal. ⚡

📐 Graph theory angle: we model the neighborhood as a weighted graph where intersections are vertices and streets are edges (often weighted by distance or travel cost). The meeting point acts like a “convergence certificate,” reducing explored area compared to single-direction search—especially useful on large, real-world road graphs.
